facts.text: Shelter Island Heights began as a late‑19th‑century Methodist summer retreat, making it one of the East End’s most distinctive historic destinations.
Shelter Island Heights was listed on both the U.S. and New York State Registers of Historic Places in 1993, preserving its 1872‑era landscape.
The hamlet’s marina culture and ferry links make it a quiet coastal spot between Long Island’s North Fork and South Fork.
Shelter Island Heights is best known for its Victorian‑era homes, cottages, inns, and tree‑lined streets that echo its historic charm.
Historic preservation, marina culture, ferry access, and coastal scenery keep Shelter Island Heights a distinctive destination on eastern Long Island.
In 1996, Perlman and his wife Toby launched the Perlman Music Program on Shelter Island, enriching the island’s cultural scene.
